newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Chemical mulls ethylene output cuts.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Chemical mulls ethylene output cuts.

text.p: Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it may join Mitsubishi Chemical Corp in cutting ethylene production to counter high naphtha prices.
"We are considering various measures to tackle high naphtha prices and dwindling profit margins, including cuts in ethylene output," a Sumitomo Chemical spokesman told Reuters.
Mitsubishi Chemical, the largest petrochemical firm in east Asia, said on Wednesday morning it would cut ethylene output by 10 percent starting in January due to soaring naphtha prices.
Naphtha is used as feedstock for ethylene production.
The Sumitomo Chemical spokesman said further discussion would be required before any decision was made on possible production cuts.
Most other top Japanese petrochemical firms, however, are not planning to trim ethylene output, company spokesmen said.
"We won't cut output unless demand for our petrochemical products slows down," a Showa Denko KK spokesman said.
Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd, Maruzen Petrochemical Co Ltd, Tonen Chemical Corp and Sanyo Petrochemical Co Ltd also said they are not considering a cut in ethylene production at present.
Mitsubishi Chemical and Sumitomo Chemical have annual ethylene production capacity of about 1.45 million tonnes and 550,000 tonnes, respectively.
